title: SO THAT YOU MAY TELL YOUR CHILDREN

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the Lord said to Moses, "Go to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and the hearts of his officials so that I may perform these signs of mine among them that you may tell your children and grandchildren how I dealt harshly with the Egyptians and how I performed my signs among them, and that you may know that I am the Lord."" - Exodus 10:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gives a purpose here we might not expect. All of this, He says, is so that you may tell your children and grandchildren.

The exodus was never meant to be a private experience. It was meant to be told. God was creating a story that parents would pass to children, who would pass it to their own children, until it reached us reading it today.

That should change how we think about our own lives. What God has done for you is not just for you. Your rescue, your answered prayers, your years of being carried — these are meant to be spoken about.

Many of us are shy about this. We think our testimony is too ordinary, or we worry about sounding boastful. But telling what God has done is not boasting about ourselves; it is boasting about Him.

The psalmist said it plainly: one generation commends God's works to another (Ps 145:4). Someone told you. Whom will you tell?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has God done in my life that I have never told anyone?
2. Which child or younger believer could I tell this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for what You have done in my life. Give me courage and words to pass it on to the next generation. Amen.
